answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a refundable bond and allocate voting power in proportion to bonded value. Splitting one bond among a thousand identities creates a plume of aliases but no extra votes, so the hollow crowd gains no leverage. To control a majority, an attacker must lock more capital than all honest voters combined and forgo its use elsewhere. The bond is the market’s basalt foundation: influence rests on costly collateral.
